svg.title: The simulated single-sided proton CT scanner, seen from above, to scale
svg.text: The simulated scanner, seen from above, to scale
Beam nozzle (y = −500 mm): pencil beams of 330 MeV protons,
spot after spot, 7 mm apart, within x ±196 mm and z ±56 mm;
spot σ 3.7 mm at the front plane. The beam log gives each proton’s spot.
the abdomen (a patient CT), turned 1° between views: 360 views;
its middle slice, with the kidneys and the liver; every voxel’s RSP is known
where each proton leaves, and in which direction
calorimeter: 75 layers, 5.5 mm apart, each of ALPIDE pixel chips and 3.5 mm of aluminium
where the proton stops gives its range, and so its WEPL
z, the rotation axis: out of the page
No detector before the patient: the scanner knows a proton’s entry only from its spot.
